description: Figure 4 is a bar chart illustrating the proportion (as a percentage) of incorrectly answered samples where the popularity of model-generated entities (Pop_Ge) and ground-truth entities (Pop_GT) differ, alongside the proportion of correctly answered samples where Pop_GT (which is also Pop_Ge in correct cases) is observed. The chart is organized into three main categories on the x-axis: “Movies,” “Songs,” and “Basketball.” For each category, there are three grouped bars representing three different LLMs: Llama3 (blue), Qwen2 (red), and ChatGPT (yellow), as indicated by the legend. The y-axis is labeled “Ratio (%)” and ranges from 50 to 90, with tick marks at intervals of 10. In the “Movies” category, Llama3 and Qwen2 both show high ratios (~90%), while ChatGPT is lower (~72%). In “Songs,” Llama3 is ~84%, Qwen2 is ~89%, and ChatGPT is ~62%. In “Basketball,” Llama3 is ~67%, Qwen2 is ~57%, and ChatGPT is ~61%. The chart visually emphasizes that for incorrectly answered samples, Pop_Ge tends to be higher than Pop_GT (which is only shown for correct samples), suggesting that models often generate more popular but incorrect entities. The figure is presented with a gray placeholder above it, indicating that the actual visual content of Figure 4 may be missing or replaced in this version of the document.
